1363.html: KINDERGARTEN SCHLUDERNS Child-friendly and sustainable: With the Schluderns kindergarten, Roland Baldi Architects realized a wooden building with a gable roof, plastered facade and significant, differently sized windows, which with their staggered arrangement and dimension are reminiscent of an oversized children’s drawing. Inside, all rooms are accessed via the spacious, light-filled foyer, which is also a welcome, recreation and play area.

Civil defense center Ritten Saving architecture, stamped out of concrete: With the new building of the Civil Defense Center Ritten, Roland Baldi Architects have built a joint home for the fire department, the mountain rescue service and the White Cross, which creates cross-competence conditions for smooth operations. The two-story structure, built as Klimahaus A, was integrated into the natural course of the terrain and communicates with the main street running there and the residential zone behind it via the north-facing entrance area. Most of the volume, however, was arranged in a compact structure below the parking lot.
Photos © Oskar Da Riz

1353.html: AMOLARIS Private Garden Chalets & Residence The task was to build 8 chalets and a small restaurant to extend the former Residence Obermühle (founded in 1970). In addition to the given architectural goals, it was also a concern of the client to implement an ecological and natural construction method. Together with executing companies, which come exclusively from South Tyrol, a high-quality and energy-efficient object could be built.

1352.html: The Rubner farm Peter Rubner runs a farm in the municipality of Kiens in South Tyrol. In a fantastic location. With one foot integrated in the village structure, with the other foot in the green.

Villa Paola A small villa stands in a relatively large garden. The owners of the villa decide to sell part of the garden. The construction company Puntel acquires the property and commissions us with the planning. The location of the property is very interesting. It is located a few steps away from the center and yet you can live there like in a small garden settlement. This also shows that we are often asked where this house with the curved balconies is actually located: in the middle of Bruneck and you can’t find it.
Photos © wisthaler.com

1362.html: Apartment house Parc Hotel Sulden The appearance of the new building fits into the typical for this area – small hamlet structure with individually conditioned building orientations, details and characteristics. The architectural characteristics of these buildings will be characterized mainly by the materials, the appropriate details and by the spatial and functional requirements of the construction task: Guest apartments with the outdoor areas in the form of terraces on the upper floors (upper floor and first floor 2) in wooden construction. Company apartments, reception areas, ancillary rooms on the lower floors (first floor 2 / first floor 1) realized in solid construction (reinforced concrete and masonry) with a surface adapted to the local building tradition, such as mineral plaster or stone surfaces.

The project for the new village square with inn in Covelano is part of the competition “Ortsraumgestaltung Schlanders 2020”, which was won in 2014. One of the areas covered was Covelano, a fraction of the municipality of Silandro, located a little off the main roads but directly on the national network of cycle paths. Covelano has its own marble quarry, the Covelano marble, which is very profitable for the village and which the village community is rightly proud of. The competition area in Covelano included an ensemble-protected central area with an old fire station with forecourt as a maneuvering area, but which had been unused for more than 20 years.
Photos © Samuel Holzner

Residence Winzerhöhe “How to deal with an existing building whose architectural qualities turn out to be rather modest and whose stylistic execution no longer meets the expectations; what can be realized with the given budget and how to succeed in developing a clear, harmonious and contemporary concept for a new operation with the given framework conditions.” These were the questions faced by builders and planners at the start of the project. The planning was preceded by many discussions and a thorough analysis of the existing situation, at some point it was clear what was wanted, now it was up to the architects to find tools to turn these ideas into reality.
Photos © Benjamin Pfitscher

“How to deal with an existing building whose architectural qualities turn out to be rather modest and whose stylistic execution no longer meets the expectations; what can be realized with the given budget and how to succeed in developing a clear, harmonious and contemporary concept for a new operation with the given framework conditions.”

Residential house Ofenbaur The existing Gasthof Ofenbaur will be demolished and subsequently a terraced residential complex will be realized. Architectural Concept Terrace Housing: Due to the ideal nature of the existing slope formation, the idea for this project was to apply the concept of terrace housing. With terracing, the building volumes can be gently embedded into the natural terrain following the current slope. The terracing offers the advantage that all residential units have a spacious terrace in front.
Photos © Alexa Rainer

1343.html: House Barbian The semi-detached house is situated on a small and very narrow plot. The height difference of the terrain is two and a half stories between the entrance area with the garage and the natural terrain at the back of the building. That is why the house develops upwards in mezzanines. A glazed recess illuminates the centrally located stairwell and provides access to the individual levels. Also above the staircase, a large horizontal window provides natural lighting from above. Only the rooms and bathrooms are separated with doors, the rest is a single public space with different functions and living spaces on each level. Thus, the house gets a strong reference to the outdoor space with views and small open spaces.

1345.html: Residence P. During planning, great attention was paid to a natural integration of the building into the natural terrain. On a slope above the promenade that leads from Oberbozen to Lichtenstern lies the residential house with an imposing view of the Rosengarten. The residential house was built in the climate house A – standard.

1355.html: Hotel Plunhof The Wellness Hotel Plunhof is located in Ridnaun near Sterzing. The 4-star superior hotel is managed by the Volgger family, composed of eight siblings and mother Paula, under the motto “Home of the generations” is one of the most renowned wellness hotels in South Tyrol. In addition, the hotel has an EU Ecolabel certification and a climate hotel pre-certification, which will be completed in the course of the realization of the next construction lot, which is currently being planned. The architectural design of the conversion focuses on two themes: The connection to the centuries-old mining tradition of the location, which was implemented through the choice of materials and the integration of targeted design elements, as well as the connection to nature through the large-scale window elements with flowing transitions between inside and outside, as well as unique panoramic views of the mountains of Ridnaun.

Office partnership Planwerk The headquarters of the office community Planwerk.it is the result of close cooperation between five technical freelancers in the district of Sterzing. The design of the single-story building emphasizes an open, bright environment for daily work and collaboration.
Facts / Figures:
Client: Bürogemeinschaft Planwerk.it : Arch. Bastian Helfer – Ing. Gianluca Cordani – Arch.int. Kurt Eisendle – Geom. Jürgen Salzburger – Ing. Artur Braunhofer
Year of manufacture: 2019-2020
Climate house class: A
Photos © Bastian Helfer

1342.html:
Cirna – Gentle Luxury Logdes
The concept To convey exquisite vacation moments, moments that remain in memory and give pleasure, to offer their guests exactly the space and comfort that each individual needs for themselves to gather new energies, that is the goal that the Linter family, which already runs the Apartments Schwarzlehen in the second generation, has set itself. Unique, natural and full of strength as it is the natural landscape that surrounds the “Cirna”, so should be the vacation that the guest spends in the new lodges of the family. Values such as independence, freedom, restraint, down-to-earthness and sustainability are the supporting pillars in the family members’ personal dealings with each other and with their guests.

1337.html: Bar Lions Mals Löwen Bar, welcoming, elegant and immersed in an atmosphere of the past, becomes the perfect meeting place to relax. A lounge designed to enjoy a drink, where it is important to drink well and feel at home in a space where you can live freely and discover the quality of the precious raw materials of our land and the excellence and design from around the world. The result is a club where areas of different shapes, color schemes and a mix of materials and finishes offer flexible comfort and a recognizable, welcoming and familiar place.

H&T The single-family house in Mals (BZ) inspires with its special location and the holistic conception.The fantastic view of the Ortler mountains in combination with the consistent design creates a home with the highest design standards. From one source and without compromise. Like a red thread, the overall atmosphere runs through all rooms of the house and perfectly reflects the personality and lifestyle of the owners. Inspiration and design guideline of this object is the play with surfaces, natural shapes and reduced lines – wood, lacquer, metal, stone and glass in combination create the extravagant overall image.
Photos ©

1321.html: Symbiosis of architecture and ecology –House Tasser-Nocker at the “Unterhuberhof” in Reischach (Bruneck) During the planning phase, several variants were played out in a goal-oriented dialogue – “ping-pong” – until it was possible to decide on the final room program, the construction method and the materiality. The originally planned “pure” wooden house became a wooden post and beam building with clay brick infill and clay plaster.

1338.html: Alphotel Tyrol CLOSE TO NATURE – REGIONAL – SUSTAINABLE The architecture makes use of natural materials. Wood and stone are the main actors of the design and form a unity with the surrounding landscape. Other natural materials such as clay, wool and glass are determinants of the overall design. The wood used comes from the valley. Built in traditional wooden construction and covered with typical local “shingles”, the forest chalets live up to their name.

Tradition, naturalness and spirit of renewal characterize the architectural image of the farm. The Integration into the surrounding landscape and the new purpose of the farmstead determine the design. Efficient energy use and the resulting living comfort play a decisive role in the implementation of the new farmstead.
Photos © Architects Haller & Ohnewein

RESIDENTIAL COMPLEX “OLYMPIA A SYMBIOSIS OF STRAIGHT AND SWEEPING In the middle of Sterzing you can find the housing estate OLYMPIA. Very thoughtful and subtle, the design language of the building stands out from the surrounding residential buildings. A symbiosis of straight and sweeping lines draw a memorable design and determine the appearance
Photos © Architects Haller & Ohnewein

This includes the Kreuzberg Pass, which at 1,636m above sea level is the easternmost gateway to the nature park and an important starting point for numerous hiking tours and other leisure activities in the mountains.
Photos © Gustav Willeit

1395.html:
Hotel Am Sonnenhang
Demolition and reconstruction hotel “Am Sonnenhang In the center of Dorf Tirol the former hotel “Tirolerhof” was demolished and rebuilt and now forms together with the adjacent residence “Am Sonnenhang” the new hotel residence complex “Am Sonnenhang”. The hotel was certified as a climate house “A”. It is terraced and has large window fronts on the south side. The terraces are arranged in such a way that in summer, when the sun is high, the terraces above guarantee shading and protect against overheating. In winter, on the other hand, the low-lying sun can warm the rooms unhindered and solar gains can be used.

1407.html:
Presulis Lodge The owners Sylvia Mairhofer and Goller Meinhard had the desire to expand the old inn “Pröslerhof” qualitatively and quantitatively and to create a unique vacation ambience with modern and special vacation apartments. For this purpose, part of the land to the west of the old house was rezoned to a tourism zone.
The buildings were designed in climate house standard A and without living space ventilation.

1340.html: Butchery & Enotheque Bernardi Where once the grain for the old Bruneck hospital was ground, there is now a carefully restored building where, among other things, the bacon of the Bernardi butchery hangs out. The rest of the building was restored to its original design after several reconstructions in the past.

Mountain Residence Montana The Residence Montana is located in a wonderful position on the edge of a small rural settlement in the Val Casies.Over the years, the family business has been repeatedly expanded and modernized. Thus, two older buildings were replaced by a new structure. Spacious apartments, private apartment, foyer, garage and a large panoramic swimming pool was newly built and attached to an existing building. Proportions, materials, choice of colors, roof pitch as well as the embedding in the steeply sloping terrain seek the context to the existing buildings.
Photos © Lukas Auer

Plumbing Messner The annex is an extension of the existing premises of the Messner plumbing company. Thanks to the additional cubage, new storage, office and exhibition space could be created. A spacious company apartment has been placed in the attic. A compact and simple structure was docked to the existing building on the street side. The structure reflects the company’s field of activity through the use of sheet metal and metal sheeting.
Photos © Gustav Willeit

Residence Cierzo Next to a large rural building on the valley floor of the Gsiesertal, there is a small residential volume as an extension for the young generation. Out of respect for the tranquil status quo, the proportions, roof pitches, articulation and materials were replicated and reinterpreted in the new building. Despite its smallness, the floor plan conveys a feeling of spaciousness. The simple volume with a high level of detail is a sign of the independence of the new building.
Photos © Gustav Willeit

Apartment H The architecture of the private apartment seeks the play between open sequences of spaces with smooth transitions and areas of retreat. The area of the central kitchen-cum-living-room, complete with piano and a “Schlemme” table, is in direct context with the terrace, which functions as an extended living space in the warmer months of the year. The choice of finishes was consistently reduced to oak wood, black steel, white plaster and doors, and trowelled floors.
Photos © Gustav Willeit

1324.html: Aparthotel Panorama Living in Meransen The project envisages a terraced building that is restrainedly transverse to the Slope developed downward in three stages. There is an unobstructed view of the valley to the south from the road above. The part of the building that runs parallel to the slope embeds itself in the terrain and literally disappears into it. The complex is oriented towards the valley, the apartments have for the most part an unobstructed view to the south and towards the Puster Valley.

The project envisages the construction of a residential building with a private apartment or 4 vacation apartments and the required agricultural buildings (stable, barn, machine hall, farm store, etc.).
Photos © Hannes Niederkofler

1323.html: CAFÉ RESTAURANT CENTRAL Remodeling & Design Klobenstein am Ritten, 2019 In the course of remodeling and redesigning the aging premises, an inviting and functional inn will be created. To provide the space with more daylight, the existing arched windows on the west and south facades will be opened to the floor and replaced with new glazing. Thus, these facades continue the existing arcade on the north facade of the building. The arched openings on the street-side west façade provide an inviting effect that enlivens the village scene through the increased visual references between the public space and the bar. On the south façade, the generous glazing with wicker awnings extends the restaurant area to include a sunny garden with a wooden terrace, which is now accessible through wooden doors integrated into the sides of the arches.

Klobenstein am Ritten, 2019 Casa Luis is a residence for a young family of six. Their desire for the best views and light, privacy and generous open spaces was as much a design consideration as the morphological nature of the site, sunlight and development guidelines. Neighboring properties are built on to the south and north, and a road runs past the southwest side. Wooded hills, gently sloping meadows and natural stone walls characterize towards the northeast the gentle wide landscape against the background of the mountain panorama of the Dolomites.
Photos © Karina Castro

1316.html: Slope to nature The building is situated in the middle of a sensitive natural landscape, surrounded by forest and chestnut groves. The log house, built in the 1960-ies, had a size of 170m3. The construction task was to demolish the log house and place a new structure in the garden area. The clients’ aspiration was to treat the garden, which had grown over decades, with care and to create a contemporary living situation.

1339.html: Philosophy “We build with local materials, local craftsmen and the characters of the people who live here. It’s not an intellectual issue, it’s an emotional issue: we want to give our projects the opportunity to age gracefully.” For pedevilla architects, building means consciously dealing with social, cultural, economic and ecological components of everyday life. The integration of a building into existing local structures plays just as important a role as responding to the respective temperature and climate influences. In this context, the issue of consistency becomes an important factor in planning decisions. “We are concerned with the cycles of the materials used, their durability and service life, but also with traditional craftsmanship methods that have been handed down, with knowledge that was thought to be lost; but above all, we are concerned with the fact that materials live.”

Client: Aqua Bad Cortina – Alberti Mutschlechner family
Place: San Vigilio di Marebbe / South Tyrol
Cubature: 920 m³
Project and realization: 2018-2019 “Without insulation – only solid wood from the storm Vaja”. The ciAsa (Rhaeto-Romanic for house) is a high alpine all-wood residential house in St.Vigil in South Tyrol, surrounded by the Val Badia Dolomites. It stands on a gentle hill, right next to a thermal spring.

Place: Bressanone/South Tyrol
Total area: 800 m² Project and realization: 2018-2019 The new inn is located in the old town of Bressanone in the immediate vicinity of the cathedral. The structural beginnings of the building date back to the 13th century. Among other things, it was the official residence of the cathedral dean. Several successive historic interiors can accommodate up to a hundred people, a courtyard and sunny garden complement the hospitality business.
Photos © Gustav Willeit

Hotel BühelwirtSt. Jakob in Ahrntal / South Tyrol The existing building sits on the Bühel at 1200m above sea level and was extended to the east on the land below. The extension extends over 6 floors and is positioned in the north of the site so as not to restrict the existing structure in its use, in terms of visual relationships and sunlight. The asymmetrically placed gable roof also cleverly plays off the recreational spaces in the existing building and at the same time responds to the urban conditions.
Photos © Gustav Willeit

1336.html: Hotel Saltus Take a breath, feel relaxation, enjoy the forest and experience grounding – that was the formulated program for the newly built Hotel Saltus in Jenesien near Bolzano. Every single choice of material, every design decision was subordinated to this content-related requirement. And in the end, all the pieces came together to form a coherent whole.

Stadele Rooms The Stadele Rooms fits into the village development between Aichweg and Gartenstrasse in Lana as a well-studied fitting piece. Fits and fits perfectly. The building stands there like a monolith of concrete, a monolith that has shaken off all decorative accessories and becomes a piece of jewelry itself. On its bright, velvet surface, climb space-creating dark balcony boxes.
Photos © DPerbellini

1322.html: Prunner Luxury Suites “With the “Prunner Luxury Suites” project in Schenna, we have realized a synthesis between architecture and rural life, a fused structure between nature and urban space.” UPC – Architects
“With the “Prunner Luxury Suites” project in Schenna, we have realized a synthesis between architecture and rural life, a fused structure between nature and urban space.”

1330.html: Philosophy noa* is an award-winning architecture and design studio founded in 2011 by Lukas Rungger and Stefan Rier, based in Bolzano (Italy), Berlin (Germany) and since 2022 also in Milan (Italy). noa* stands for the essential expression of a collaborative work ethic: the young team of architects, designers and artists relies on an interdisciplinary design methodology that is in constant flux depending on the requirements of each project. The concept of “emergence”, where the whole is far more than the sum of its parts, becomes the central strategy of a holistic approach to any design conceived by noa*. NOA*… THE NETWORK OF INTERNATIONALLY ACTIVE CREATIVE MINDS

Boundaries – between past and future, between dream and reality, between inside and outside: noa* makes the invisible lines visible, part of the whole, and above all, instead of a separation, a connection between two worlds.
Photo ©Alex Filz

If architecture adopts the vibrancy and diversity of nature, it will never be perceived as a foreign body. noa* has integrated elements for a special hotel project that awaken memories, dreams and perhaps even a bit of a sense of adventure in every guest.
Photo ©Alex Filz

It was the famous leap into the deep end: how noa* succeeded with a great deal of flair at the idyllic Völser Weiher lake to tie in with a cherished tradition with a new, modern concept and at the same time harmoniously harmonize architecture with nature.
Photo ©Alex Filz

1315.html: The term sustainability is on everyone’s lips – as architects, we bear responsibility in this sense:

Design decisions in terms of materiality, form, size, use, flexibility, orientation, social embedding … ideally allow a built environment to emerge that contributes to being able to live and experience the future in a positive way – regardless of scale. Plasma Studio tries in its work – from the design object to the master planning – to appropriately meet site, building task, user and context: there is no recipe for this. With the joy of experimentation, we try to do justice to the future in every project.
